title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Invoice Disputes and Their Grounds
content:
## Who disputes, and what

Each dispute on a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record is aimed at a single invoice line, and raising one is reserved to the billed party. Lodging is the customer's act; deciding falls to the desk, which has the product's response time to do so.

## Time limit

To be in time, a dispute must reach the desk within the product's dispute window, which runs in calendar days from the issue date of the invoice concerned.

- The window is anchored on the invoice date the account entry shows.
- Adding the product's window days to that date, on the calendar, gives the window's final day.
- Lodging on that final day still counts as in time; lodging a day later does not.

## One dispute per line

A line can bear a single dispute only; any dispute already on it whose outcome is submitted, upheld, partially upheld or denied uses up that one place.

## Grounds and how each is decided

| Ground put forward | How the desk decides it |
|---|---|
| issued after the invoicing deadline | Decided from the records. Where the line's date falls after its invoicing deadline — the day charges stopped accruing, advanced by the product's deadline days — the desk finds for the customer and the line cannot be collected. What clears it is a waiver entered under the reason late invoice rather than any dispute credit, and a customer who simply draws attention to a late line, with no formal dispute, has it cleared by that same kind of waiver. |
| rates misapplied, or free time misapplied | Decided from the records. The desk recomputes the line under the invoicing rules with the product on the record and the recorded dates. Where the invoiced figure exceeds the recomputation, the dispute succeeds in whole or in part and the difference is credited, capped at the amount the customer disputed; where it does not exceed it, the dispute is denied and nothing is booked. |
| movement dates contested, delay caused by the line, terminal closure | The answer depends on operational facts that lie outside the desk's records, so the desk records such a dispute without being able to decide it. |

## Retired wording

For a demurrage invoice line, the former wording that a late invoice is cleared by a late-invoice waiver of the **whole** amount still open on it is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for clearing a late demurrage line. A late detention line continues to be cleared of the whole amount still open on it, that is its invoiced amount less every waiver and credit already booked against it.

## Further clauses

- Dispute credits and waiver entries alike require the record to show invoiced at the time they are booked.
- An invoice does not fall due for as long as a dispute against it remains submitted.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, 25-day window assumed for illustration)

- Invoice dated 5 August, dispute lodged 30 August: in time, the window's last day.
- The same invoice, dispute lodged 31 August: out of time.

superseded_clauses: the whole amount still open on the invoice is cleared by a dnd_charge_waived row with waiver_reason late_invoice
